svg.title: Propagate headers on outbound calls
svg.desc: Two checkout requests, A and B, are in flight at once, and each one's duplicated context holds its X-Correlation-Id and X-Box-Office values. When checkout() calls the payment provider through the PaymentClient REST client, the client's ClientHeadersFactory reads the values from the context of the request that made the call and puts them on POST /charges as headers. A's call reaches the provider with 7f3a and web, and B's call with c41e and kiosk.
svg.text: Propagate headers on outbound calls
A ClientHeadersFactory copies the headers in each request's duplicated context onto the calls that request makes.
checkout()
POST /checkout
stored by the request filter
PaymentClient
@RegisterClientHeaders
payment provider
remote service
A
B
Requests A and B are in checkout(). Each one's duplicated context already holds its headers.
A's checkout() calls charge() on PaymentClient, the REST client for the payment provider.
Before the call leaves, the client runs its ClientHeadersFactory, which reads A's context.
update() returns 7f3a and web as headers, and POST /charges carries them to the provider.
B's checkout() calls charge() while the provider is still handling A's call.
The same factory runs for B's call, reads B's context, and returns c41e and kiosk.
B's call leaves with c41e and kiosk, and A's call still carries 7f3a and web.
One factory serves both calls, but each call carries the headers of the request that made it.
Sources: quarkus.io/guides/rest-client (custom headers support) and quarkus.io/guides/duplicated-context (context local data).
